anchor_case_definition.note_on_matrix_choice: count5.c is AES-NI hardware-only and cannot run any matrix other than the real AES MixColumns matrix; the anchor is therefore necessarily run under AES_MC, not BATCH-002's M0/M1 zero-entry substitutes.

prediction.basis: AES_MC has no zero entries in any row/column, so per the reviewed round-split derivation (CORR-20260802-46b73b) the r=4 property HOLDS at every j0 under this matrix.

prediction.order_of_magnitude: ~2^31 (approx 2.1-2.2e9), by analogy with BATCH-001's other AES_MC r=5 arms at different keys
prediction.exact_n: not predicted in advance; no prior committed record measured this exact (key, base, r=5, AES_MC) combination
prediction.basis: CORR-20260802-46b73b: at r=5 the no-zero-entry hypothesis is dispensable; a non-singular column-preserving mixing layer (AES_MC qualifies) is the correct hypothesis, so the property should still read 0 mod 8.

CASE_NZ_r5_nonzero_expected.note: n = 2147544888 is exact and bit-for-bit identical between the two independently-written engines, including all 13 non-empty histogram bins. This is a substantially stronger anchor than the zero case: two buggy engines could coincidentally both read zero, but coincidental agreement on a specific 10-digit count plus an identical 13-bin histogram is not a plausible artifact of independent bugs.

verdict.statement: THE CROSS-INSTRUMENT ANCHOR CLOSES THIS CONFOUND, WITHIN THE TESTED SCOPE. On the same key, base, j0 and matrix, count5.c (BATCH-001, AES-NI-hardware engine) and cnt.c (BATCH-002, software T-table engine) agree EXACTLY -- same N, same n, same n_alt, same n_mod8, same max_occ, and IDENTICAL full occupancy histograms -- on both a case predicted and measured as exactly zero (r=4) and a case measured as a specific large 10-digit non-zero count (r=5, n=2147544888) that was NOT predicted to the digit in advance. No disagreement was found.
verdict.consequence_for_EV-AES-005_and_EV-AES-d3: The specific unresolved confound named in EV-AES-d33b1c OBS-B2-3 ('The cross-instrument anchor against BATCH-001's engine was never run') is now discharged by a measurement, for the tested case (r in {4,5}, j0=0, AES_MC matrix, one key/base pair, this machine, this compiler/build). This does not retroactively verify cnt.c's behavior on BATCH-002's own M0/M1 zero-entry matrices -- count5.c cannot run those matrices at all, so no cross-instrument check of THOSE specific matrices is possible with count5.c as the second instrument; that residual gap is named explicitly below, not glossed over.
does_not_establish: That cnt.c's M0/M1 zero-entry-matrix arms (BATCH-002 segment 3, and the M1 arms TASK-20260804-fdafdf was dispatched to re-examine) are correct -- count5.c cannot run a non-standard matrix, so this anchor cannot reach those specific arms.
Anything about full-round or deployed AES; no comparison to published cryptanalysis in either direction (RQ-AES-003 R3).
Agreement at other keys, bases, round counts, thread counts, or window configurations, which were not tested.
